_about: Inputs for scripts/simulate_district.py. Every output of that script is SIMULATED. Brief figures keep TODO(source) until the owner supplies the papers; their study settings may differ from ours. Screening, not diagnosis.

children.source: Design choice: a round district-sized cohort for illustration.

screening_coverage.source: ASSUMPTION: every enrolled child with consent is screened. Real coverage (absence, consent) TODO(source) from a pilot.

prevalence.source: Challenge brief: 14.14% of school children. TODO(source): the study, its definition of hearing loss and its setting.

screen_sensitivity.source: ASSUMPTION: ideal screen, so the funnel isolates follow-up. Swept 0.7-1.0. Rule-logic estimates on US data: scripts/eval_nhanes.py (not field accuracy).

screen_specificity.source: ASSUMPTION: ideal screen (no false referrals). Swept 0.85-1.0. See scripts/eval_nhanes.py for rule-logic estimates on US data.

follow_up.source: Challenge brief: 39.4% of referred children followed up with SMS reminders only; 88.5% when ear camps were held at school. TODO(source) for both: study, setting, what 'followed up' means. Our app implements the camp model (camp request, missed-camp reminder, case tracking); we have no data showing it reaches 88.5%.

value.school_camp: Referral + ear camp at school (what this app organises)

models.source: Design choice: the two follow-up models in the brief.

monte_carlo.source: ASSUMPTION: illustrative uncertainty ranges, not from data. Each run draws prevalence, sensitivity and specificity uniformly from these ranges and each follow-up rate uniformly within +/- follow_up_spread (clipped to 0-1), then binomial counts.
